- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” lag: subtract 1–2% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast decline by 2–5% to align with sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–8%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average filter.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a low, model often misses the rally; add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment turns bullish within 3 days.
